chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: John Kirby: tuba, steel string bass and his own sextet
summary: Kirby, later married to Maxine Sullivan, played tuba with Fletcher, had a six-piece hotel combo and a metal string bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Next in line here is John Kirby, whom you've mentioned already.

John Kirby. Now there's a guy. He was a real character. You know, John was married to the great singer, Maxine Sullivan. In later years this happened. But John had a great little six piece combo that played some of the major hotels in the country. That was a great group. In fact, that's -- he was a great tuba player originally, and he played tuba with Fletcher starting out, but he also played the string bass. And he was one of the few bass players that had a string bass that was a tin. When I say tin, you know, steel. It wasn't one of those wooden basses.
Oh, yes. It's metal. Metal, uh-huh.
Metal is the word, but I said tin.
